blueprint_inputs.why: Barrel%, pull-air and FB% predict HR beyond past HR.
Bat speed gives early power signal.
Pitcher's HR/FB and barrels allowed by hand.
Park HR factor by handedness and weather.
Wind component along pull-side field.
Air density and altitude: lower air density reduces drag and increases ball carry, raising HR and scoring (Denver, hot days).
Handedness matchup: same-handed matchups favour pitchers (especially vs breaking balls), opposite-handed matchups favour hitters, and the size of the split differs by player.
PA count multiplier: pA count is the volume multiplier for hits, TB, HR, RBI and runs, and depends on the lineup slot, the team's run environment and the opposing pitcher.
Regress HR/FB luck: home runs per fly ball regress strongly to a mean determined by park and contact quality, so past HR luck is not persistent.
Pitch-type matchup such as fastball hitters vs fastball-heavy pitchers.
Confirmed participation and slot.

unreg:all_star_week_events.blueprint_mechanism: HR is a rare per-PA event whose probability is the hitter's HR rate (barrels, pull-air, FB%) modified by the pitcher's HR vulnerability, platoon, park HR factor by handedness and weather (wind, temperature), multiplied across expected PAs and hits against starter and bullpen. Variance is intrinsic; HR/FB luck regresses. Small multiplicative shifts in environment matter because of the low base probability.

blueprint_inputs.why: Transaction timeline and rules.
Team standing drives trades: a team's playoff position and strategy determine whether it adds or sells players and thus the probability of a trade.
Option, 40-man and Rule 5 constraints.
Reports precede transactions: transactions and news change who plays and the team's strength with a lag before statistics catch up.
Injuries trigger call-ups and IL moves.
Playoff odds define buyer/seller state.
Reference-class frequencies: for off-field markets, history of similar announcements is the best available prior.
What counts as official transaction.
Market reaction to reports: the traded price aggregates every participant's information about this contract, including injury and lineup news that moves faster than public stats.

unreg:labour_stoppage_and_season_schedul.blueprint_mechanism: Transactions follow institutional calendars and team incentives: standing (buyer vs seller), contract status, roster rules and ownership/front-office behaviour. Reports from beat writers precede many moves. Probabilities are a hazard over the window, mostly estimated from reference classes with updates from reported news and standings.

blueprint_inputs.why: Series state, rest and rotation.
Elimination and leverage context.
Starters in the playoff rotation.
Shorter leash and high-leverage reliever usage.
Bullpen quality matters more in the postseason.
Offence vs likely starters: a team's lineup quality against the starter's handedness determines runs in the early innings, more than overall season team offence.
Key injuries before and during the series.
Home-field and bracket structure.
Talent prior: projection systems summarise multi-year talent estimates that are better priors for team strength than early-season results.
Series and game price benchmark.

unreg:playoff_series_markets.blueprint_mechanism: Series probability is a dynamic program over remaining games with per-game win probabilities that depend on announced starters, rest, bullpen availability, home-field pattern and injuries. Postseason managers shorten starter leash and use best relievers more, compressing talent gaps relative to the regular season, and rotation set by off-days matters more than ratings alone.
